title: Thumb Sign Emoji: Copy & Paste 🫹 🫺, Final in Emoji 18.0
meta_description: Leftwards and Rightwards Thumb Sign (🫹 U+1FAF9, 🫺 U+1FAFA) became final in Emoji 18.0 on September 16, 2026: sideways pointing gestures, distinct from Thumbs Up/Down. As of September 25, 2026, no phone or computer shows them by default.
hero_tagline: A directional pointing pair, not another approval gesture, final in Emoji 18.0 since Unicode 18.0's release on September 16, 2026. As of September 25, 2026, no phone or computer shows them by default, but either codepoint copies with one click.
intro: Leftwards Thumb Sign (🫹, U+1FAF9) and Rightwards Thumb Sign (🫺, U+1FAFA) are a paired set of new emoji in Emoji 18.0, the emoji companion to Unicode 18.0, which became final on September 16, 2026. Despite the name, they aren't another approval gesture alongside Thumbs Up and Thumbs Down: they're horizontal, pointing signs, closer in job to the existing Backhand Index Pointing Left/Right emoji than to a vertical thumb. The pair answers a long-running community complaint: Unicode's gesture set has always skewed toward right-handed, vertical approval signs, with no clean way to point a thumb "at this one" versus "at that one" in a reply or comparison. There's real precedent for the category: the 2021 Pushing Hand proposal already established directional hand gestures as a legitimate emoji lane beyond simple thumbs-up approval. Unicode's final emoji data gives each sign all five skin-tone modifiers, so the pair comes in 10 skin-tone variants (five each). Final status puts the pair in the standard, not yet on screens. Google has published designs for both in its Noto Color Emoji font, but as of September 25, 2026, no operating system, keyboard, or system emoji font ships them, so expect a blank box or placeholder glyph until platforms add support. For when that happens, Emojipedia's estimate, based on last year's schedule, is WhatsApp, Samsung and Google in the first quarter of 2027, Apple around March or April 2027 and Microsoft in late summer or early fall 2027.
sources: Both thumb signs, U+1FAF9 and U+1FAFA, are listed with five skin-tone versions each in Unicode 18.0's emoji-test.txt data file, published with the Unicode Consortium's Unicode 18.0 announcement on September 16, 2026. Emojipedia reported Google's Noto Color Emoji designs for Emoji 18.0 and published the 2027 rollout estimates quoted above.
